claim: Huber regression is handled via a gamma_p-loss framework in O~(r*sqrt(mn)/epsilon + poly(n,1/epsilon)) quantum time (Corollary 12).
paper: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms (arXiv:2509.24757 / OpenReview TBSyYj4VV6)
method: Leverage-score sparsifier applied to Huber (IRLS on full vs weighted sketch); m-scaling timed; asymptotic symbolic.
reason: Sparsifier (1+/-eps) embedding holds (gram rel-err=0.133<=0.15); Huber optimum on sketch within 0.50 of full (ratio=0.016). gamma_p-loss reduces each iteration to reweighted LS, which the sparsifier preserves. Classical solve slope in m = 1.37, sketch slope = -0.81. Quantum/classical -> 0. EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: literal quantum construction (QRAM) NOT executed on CPU.

mutation.description: (M1) s<r/eps^2 breaks optimum-preservation; (M2) tighter eps needs more samples; (M3) quantum sqrt(m) required for speedup.
